🌍 REAL WORLD LINK

Everything Comes From the Ground

Minerals power modern life

Your phone, your car, the wires in your walls — all started as rock dug from the Earth and processed into useful materials.

RESOURCES

What Is an Ore?

An ore is a naturally occurring material from which a valuable mineral or metal can be extracted economically
Ores are processed to separate and concentrate useful materials
Whether material is an ore depends on the deposit and extraction costs
IRON & STEEL

Iron Ore → Steel

Iron ore, coke and limestone react in a blast furnace to make iron
The iron is processed and alloyed, usually with carbon, to make steel
Steel properties can be adjusted for different uses
APPLICATIONS

Where We Use Steel

Buildings and bridges (structural beams)
Cars and trucks (body panels, engine parts)
Appliances (fridges, washing machines)
ALUMINIUM

Bauxite → Aluminium

The Bayer process refines bauxite into alumina (aluminium oxide)
Electrolysis of molten alumina uses electricity to produce aluminium
Used in cans, foil, and aircraft parts

Thermal Coal vs Coking Coal

Thermal Coal
Burned in power stations
Generates electricity
Designed to burn for heat and electricity
Coking Coal
Converted into coke
Used in steel production
Processed into coke for ironmaking
CRITICAL MINERALS

Copper and Lithium

Copper: smelted and purified → wire, pipes, circuits
Lithium: chemically processed → battery chemicals
Lithium-ion batteries power EVs, laptops, phones

Key Ideas to Remember

Ore → Process

Raw minerals need processing to become useful

Iron & Steel

Blast furnace makes iron; alloying makes steel

Aluminium

Bayer process makes alumina; electrolysis makes aluminium
